tools.name: dynatrace_managed_get_environments_info
tools.description: Get information about all connected Dynatrace Managed clusters and verify the connections and authentication services.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_list_available_metrics
tools.description:
List available metrics in the Managed cluster, optionally filtered by entity. Results include aggregation
    types, dimension definitions, and technical metadata for advanced metric analysis.

entitySelector.description:
Entity selector to filter metrics. Must use at most one entity type per query.
          Examples include:
           * type(SERVICE)
           * entityId("id1","id2")
           * type(HOST)
          Can combine with things like: entityName.contains("name"), tag("key:value"), mzName("zone").

searchText.description:
Text to search for in metric names and descriptions.
          **RECOMMENDED SEARCHES**: "response.time" (latency), "cpu.usage" (CPU), "memory" (memory),
          "error.rate" (errors), "throughput" (performance), "availability" (uptime)

limit.description:
Maximum number of metrics to return. Use this when user specifies a count
          (e.g., "first 16 metrics" → limit: 16, "500 metrics" → limit: 500).
          If not specified, returns up to API limit: 500. Cannot exceed 500

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_query_metrics_data

metricSelector.description:
Metric selector (e.g., "builtin:service.response.time" for latency,
        "builtin:tech.generic.cpu.usage" for container CPU, "builtin:host.mem.usage" for memory).
        Consider first using the tool list_available_metrics to identity the right metric.

from.description: Start time (ISO format or relative like "now-1h")

to.description: End time (ISO format or relative like "now")

resolution.description:
Data resolution. Use a bigger resolution when the timerange is larger.
          For example, use "5m" for detailed analysis of data over hour(s), use "1h" for trends of data over a day, use 6h or 1d for data over many days.

entitySelector.description:
Entity selector to filter metrics data. CRITICAL: Only ONE entity type per query.
          Use discover_entities() first to get exact names/IDs, then use entityId("exact-id") or
          type(SERVICE),entityName.equals("exact-name"). Examples: entityId("SERVICE-123"),
          type(SERVICE),entityName("payment-service"), type(AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION),tag("AWS_REGION:us-west-2")

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_get_metric_details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific metric.

metricId.description: The metric ID to get details for

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_query_logs
tools.description:
Search logs using simple text queries. Results include event types, expanded metadata fields
    (up to 8 fields), and enhanced error detection. Managed clusters support basic text search but
    not structured syntax like "content:" or "loglevel:".

query.description:
Simple text to search for in log content (e.g., "error", "exception", "timeout").
          Do NOT use structured syntax like "content:error" - just use "error".

from.description: Start time (ISO format or relative like "now-1h")

to.description: End time (ISO format or relative like "now")

limit.description: Maximum number of logs to return (default: 100). Cannot exceed 1000

sort.description: Sort order for logs. Use "-timestamp" for most recent first.

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_list_events
tools.description:
List events from the Managed cluster within a specified timeframe. Results include event properties,
    management zones, severity/impact levels, and detailed metadata for comprehensive analysis.

from.description: Start time (ISO format or relative like "now-1h")

to.description: End time (ISO format or relative like "now")

eventType.description:
Filter by event type (e.g., "CONTAINER_RESTART" for certain container issues,
          "CUSTOM_DEPLOYMENT" for deployments, "RESOURCE_CONTENTION_EVENT" for resource issues)

entitySelector.description:
Entity selector to filter events. CRITICAL: Only ONE entity type per query.
          Use discover_entities() first to get exact names/IDs, then use entityId("exact-id") or
          type(SERVICE),entityName.equals("exact-name"). Examples: entityId("SERVICE-123"),
          type(SERVICE),entityName("payment-service"), type(AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION),tag("AWS_REGION:us-west-2")

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return. Use this when user specifies a count (e.g., "first 20 events" → limit: 20). If not specified, returns up to API limit: 100. Cannot exceed 100

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_discover_entities
tools.description:
Discover entities in the Managed cluster using EntitySelector syntax. REQUIRED: Must specify
    entitySelector with exactly ONE entity type only. Results include entity properties, tags,
    management zones, and relationship counts for comprehensive topology analysis.

entitySelector.description:
Entity selector to filter the entities. CRITICAL: Must include exactly ONE entity type
          like type("SERVICE") - multiple types NOT supported. Examples: type("SERVICE"),
          entityId("ID1"), entityName.contains("name"), entityName.equals("exact"), tag("key:value"), mzName("zone"),
          healthState("HEALTHY").

mzSelector.description:
Optional management zone selector to further scope the query. Use mzId(123,456) for zone IDs
          or mzName("Bookstore-FS","Stocks") for zone names. Can combine: mzId(123),mzName("Production").
          Works alongside entitySelector.

from.description: Start time for entity observation timeframe (ISO format or relative like "now-3d")

to.description: End time for entity observation timeframe (ISO format or relative like "now")

limit.description: Maximum number of entities to return. Use this when user specifies a count (e.g., "first 10 entities" → limit: 10). If not specified, returns up to API limit: 10. Cannot exceed 50

sort.description: Sort order for entities. Use "name" for ascending, "-name" for descending by display name.

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_list_problems
tools.description: List problems from the Managed cluster with optional filtering.

status.description: Problem status - use "OPEN" for active issues, "CLOSED" for resolved problems

impactLevel.description: Impact level - use "SERVICE" for application issues, "INFRASTRUCTURE" for host/container problems, "APPLICATION" for user-facing issues

entitySelector.description: Entity selector to filter problems. CRITICAL: Only ONE entity type per query. Use discover_entities() first to get exact names/IDs, then use entityId("exact-id") or type(SERVICE),entityName.equals("exact-name"). Examples: entityId("SERVICE-123"), type(SERVICE),entityName("payment-service"), type(AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION),tag("AWS_REGION:us-west-2")

limit.description: Maximum number of problems to return. Use this when user specifies a count (e.g., "first 10 problems" → limit: 10). If not specified, returns up to API limit: 50. Cannot exceed 50

sort.description: Sort order. Use "+status" (open first), "-status" (closed first), "+startTime" (old first), "-startTime" (new first), or "+relevance"/"-relevance" (with text search).

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_get_problem_details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific problem including evidence details for root cause analysis, affected entities, entity tags, and management zones. Use the problemId (UUID format) from list_problems output, NOT the displayId.

problemId.description: The internal problem ID (UUID format) from list_problems - NOT the displayId (P-XXXXX)

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_list_security_problems
tools.description: List security problems and vulnerabilities from the Managed cluster. Results include package names, technology details, vulnerable components, and comprehensive risk assessment data.

riskLevel.description: Filter by risk level (NONE, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL)

entitySelector.description: Entity selector to filter vulnerabilities. CRITICAL: Only ONE entity type per query. Use discover_entities() first to get exact names/IDs, then use entityId("exact-id") or type(SERVICE),entityName.equals("exact-name"). Examples: entityId("SERVICE-123"), type(SERVICE),entityName("payment-service"), type(AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION),tag("AWS_REGION:us-west-2")

limit.description: Maximum number of security problems to return. Use this when user specifies a count (e.g., "first 25 vulnerabilities" → limit: 25). If not specified, returns up to API limit: 100. Cannot exceed 100

sort.description: Sort order. Examples: "+status" (open first), "-riskAssessment.riskScore" (highest risk first), "+firstSeenTimestamp" (newest first), "-lastUpdatedTimestamp" (recently updated first).

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_get_security_problem_details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific security problem including CVE details, affected entities, vulnerable components, code locations, and comprehensive technical analysis.

securityProblemId.description: The security problem ID (UUID format) from list_security_problems - NOT the displayId (S-XXXXX)

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_list_slos
tools.description: List Service Level Objectives (SLOs) from the Managed cluster. Results include timeframe details, management zones, error budget burn rates, and comprehensive SLO configuration data. IMPORTANT: When evaluate=true, the query must be limited to 25 or fewer results using the limit parameter.

sloSelector.description: SLO selector to filter results. Syntax: id("id-1","id-2") for SLO IDs, name("Service Availability") for exact name match (case-sensitive), healthState("HEALTHY"|"UNHEALTHY") [requires evaluate=true], text("value") for case-insensitive text search, problemDisplayName("P-12345") for problem display names, managementZone("MZ-A") or managementZoneID("123") for management zones. Combine with commas. Escape special characters ~ and " with ~.

timeFrame.description: Time frame for SLO evaluation: "CURRENT" for SLO's own timeframe, "GTF" for custom timeframe specified by from/to parameters

from.description: Start time (ISO format or relative like "now-2w"). Used when timeFrame="GTF"

to.description: End time (ISO format or relative like "now"). Used when timeFrame="GTF"

evaluate.description: Set to true to enable SLO evaluation. Required when using healthState in sloSelector.

sort.description: Sorting of SLO entries: "name" for ascending order, "-name" for descending order. Default: "name"

enabledSlos.description: Filter by SLO status: "true" for enabled SLOs only, "false" for disabled only, "all" for both. Default: "true"

showGlobalSlos.description: Include global SLOs in results regardless of other filters. Default: true

demo.description: Get demo SLOs instead of real ones. Default: false

limit.description: Maximum number of SLOs to return. Use this when user specifies a count (e.g., "first 15 SLOs" → limit: 15). If not specified, returns up to API limit: 100. Cannot exceed 100

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.

tools.name: dynatrace_managed_get_slo_details
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific SLO.

sloId.description: The SLO ID to get details for

from.description: Start time (ISO format or relative like "now-1w"). Used when timeFrame="GTF"

to.description: End time (ISO format or relative like "now"). Used when timeFrame="GTF"

timeFrame.description: Time frame for SLO evaluation: "CURRENT" for SLO's own timeframe, "GTF" for custom timeframe specified by from and to parameters

environment_alias.description: Specify which environment to be queried, by supplying the environment alias as returned by get_environments_info. Can use `ALL_ENVIRONMENTS` to retrieve data from all environments in one request to MCP.
